subject: SOC 2 & SIG/CAIQ evidence request — EU hosting and bridge letter
messages:
From: Alice Müller <alice.muller@finserv-example.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: security@finserv-example.com
Date: 2026-11-20T08:15:00Z
Subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II, SIG/CAIQ, and hosting residency clarifications

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this — FinServ is running a security review as part of our vendor onboarding. We have a few asks so our InfoSec and legal teams can sign off: 

- Current SOC 2 Type II report (full PDF) covering the most recent audit period.
- A bridge letter if the SOC 2 report does not cover the contract start date / go-live window.
- Completed SIG lite or CAIQ answers (we attached our questionnaire, v5).
- Confirmation of hosting region for Redwood hosted customers (we require EU residency for some workloads) and whether any customer data can be exported outside the EU. If you rely on any cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs, EU Standard Contractual Clauses, or equivalent), please state which and share the DPA/SCC addendum.
- Short list of evidence items we typically request: system inventory, encryption-at-rest and in-transit details, incident response contact, and backup retention policy.

Can you confirm timelines? We're hoping to get all artifacts by next Friday (Nov 27) to meet our procurement window. If any of this needs legal signing (DPA/DocuSign), please flag.

Attached: FinServ_Security_Questionnaire_v5.xlsx

Best,
Alice Müller
Security Reviewer — FinServ Ltd
[FinServ internal distribution: security@finserv-example.com]

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Müller <alice.muller@finserv-example.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-20T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II, SIG/CAIQ, and hosting residency clarifications

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. I'm looping in Marissa (security & compliance lead) and Vivek (privacy/legal) to ensure we cover everything. Quick summary of what we can provide immediately: 

- SOC 2 Type II (most recent report) — I will attach the PDF in my next email.
- Draft bridge letter can be produced; we usually draft a one-page bridge confirming there are no material changes since the last audit and listing the audit window.
- We maintain a CAIQ/consensus SIG response internally; we can export to your spreadsheet format.
- Hosting: Redwood hosted EU region is currently deployed in Frankfurt (AWS eu-central-1). For customers that require dedicated residency we have Redwood Dedicated and Private options; we can outline timelines and costs if needed.

Couple of clarifying Qs so we respond precisely: 
1) Do you require a signed DPA + SCCs prior to procurement approval or is a draft sufficient?
2) For the bridge letter, do you need confirmation that no customer data was transferred outside the EU during the audit period, or just a statement of controls and the audit dates?

I'll follow up with the SOC 2 packet and a CAIQ export by EOD.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[Attachment planned: SOC2_TypeII_2026_Q2.pdf]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Alice Müller <alice.muller@finserv-example.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T13:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II, SIG/CAIQ, and hosting residency clarifications

Jonas / Alice — quick internal note and response to Alice's Qs: 

- SOC 2 coverage: our latest SOC 2 Type II (attached) covers the period 2025-07-01 through 2026-06-30. The report is a standard AICPA SOC 2 Type II with CC and common criteria coverage; we do not publish full control testwork detail publicly but we can share the report under NDA.

- Bridge letter: we can provide a bridge letter that confirms the audit window above and states that there have been no material control changes since the report date. If the customer needs an explicit statement about data residency during the audit window ("no customer data exported outside the EU"), we can include that, but we typically couple that with the DPA language (SCCs + DPA addendum).

- Hosting / residency: Hosted (public) customers in the EU are served from eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). For customers requiring strict UK-only residency we have a roadmap for a UK region offering (planned for H1 2027) and can discuss Dedicated/Private options as near-term alternatives.

- Cross-border transfers: Redwood executes Data Processing Addenda that incorporate SCCs (standard contractual clauses) when needed; we also offer a contractual bridge addendum for customers with additional requirements. Vivek will attach the DPA/SCC language and confirm whether we need signatures before procurement.

- Evidence bundle: we'll provide system inventory, network architecture diagram (redacted), encryption summary (algorithms and key management), incident response contact, backup retention policy, and the CAIQ export. We can stage delivery: SOC2 + CAIQ today, bridge letter draft tomorrow, and DPA/DocuSign link once legal confirms final text.

I'll draft the bridge letter and follow up.

Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2_TypeII_2026_Q2.pdf]

From: Alice Müller <alice.muller@finserv-example.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: security@finserv-example.com
Date: 2026-11-21T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II, SIG/CAIQ, and hosting residency clarifications

Thanks Marissa — that helps. A few follow-ups from our InfoSec: 

- We do need either a signed DPA (DocuSign) or a letter confirming SCCs are in place prior to final procurement approval. A draft DPA is okay for preliminary review but we prefer executed agreements where possible.
- For the bridge letter, please include the explicit line: "During the audit period (2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30), Redwood Inference did not transfer customer data outside the European Economic Area except as required to provide the service under appropriate contractual safeguards." If you cannot include that exact wording, please propose alternate language.
- Can you confirm whether any third-party subprocessors (cloud infra, observability providers) are located outside the EU and, if so, which ones and how transfers are controlled?

We are aiming to complete the security review by Friday Nov 27. If you can get the SOC 2 PDF, CAIQ export and bridge letter draft by EOD Nov 22 and a DPA signing link shortly after, that will get us there.

Best,
Alice
FinServ Ltd — Vendor Risk Team
[Attachment: n/a]

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II, SIG/CAIQ, and hosting residency clarifications

Alice — thanks, we'll proceed on that timeline. Action plan: 

1) Attached: SOC2_TypeII_2026_Q2.pdf (covers 2025-07-01 -> 2026-06-30).
2) Attached: CAIQ export mapped to your spreadsheet (we'll upload the XLSX in a follow-up if you prefer an inline copy).
3) Draft bridge letter (Bridge_Letter_Redwood_20261122.docx) — POC draft attached; Marissa will update the exact residency sentence if legal requests changes.
4) DPA / SCCs: Vivek will send a DocuSign link for the DPA incorporating SCC clauses by tomorrow. Link will be via secure DocuSign: https://docusign.com/tx/0a1b2c3d4e5f
4) Subprocessor note: Primary infra (AWS eu-central-1) plus monitoring partner located in EU; global logs are routed through control-plane services under contractual safeguards — see attached short subprocessor list. We'll redact account IDs before sending to the vendor.

If you want the bridge letter to explicitly say "no customer data exported outside the EU during the audit period," please confirm and we'll include that exact sentence (Marissa: please confirm this is safe/legal to assert).

Next steps: I'll upload the SOC2 PDF and bridge letter to our secure file share and email you the download link. Expect DPA DocuSign tomorrow.

Thanks — Jonas
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
